Exploratory Data Analysis, Missingness Auditing, and Normalization

Source: vignettes/eda_and_missingness.Rmd
eda_and_missingness.Rmd

Overview

Clinical datasets and electronic health records (EHR) frequently exhibit complex missingness patterns, non-standard missing codes (e.g. "999", "NA", ""), and extreme statistical outliers. The TempleCBE package provides domain-agnostic tools to streamline exploratory data analysis (EDA), quantify missingness, normalize numerical features, and flag outliers cleanly.

library(TempleCBE)
library(dplyr)

1. Auditing Missing Data

Total Missingness with SumNa()

SumNa() counts missing values in vectors, data frames, or matrices, supporting explicit missing value codes (such as "NA" strings or empty strings):

library(TempleCBE)

# Sample vector with default and non-standard missing values
vec <- c(12, 14, NA, 999, 18, "")

# Count standard NAs
SumNa(vec)
#> [1] 1

# Count NAs including custom missing codes
SumNa(vec, na_list = c("999", ""))
#> [1] 3

Feature-Level Missingness Table

features_percent_miss() generates a detailed summary table sorted descending by missingness percentage:

# Synthetic clinical dataframe
df_clinical <- data.frame(
  patient_id = 1:6,
  age = c(45, 52, NA, 61, 38, NA),
  systolic_bp = c(120, 135, NA, 140, 118, 125),
  bmi = c(22.5, NA, 29.1, NA, 31.0, NA),
  smoker = c("No", "Yes", "", "No", "NA", "Yes"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

# Audit missingness with custom codes
features_percent_miss(df_clinical, na_list = c("", "NA"))
#> # A tibble: 5 × 5
#>   feature     SumNa SumComp PctNa PctComp
#>   <chr>       <int>   <int> <dbl>   <dbl>
#> 1 bmi             3       3 0.5     0.5  
#> 2 age             2       4 0.333   0.667
#> 3 smoker          2       4 0.333   0.667
#> 4 systolic_bp     1       5 0.167   0.833
#> 5 patient_id      0       6 0       1

Missingness Visualizations

Visualize missingness across all features using plot_features_percent_miss() or S3 plot():

# Plot feature missingness chart
plot_features_percent_miss(df_clinical)

# Plot top 3 missing features
plot_features_percent_miss(df_clinical, top_n = 3)

Or view complete missingness heatmaps with missmap():

# Render missingness heatmap
missmap(df_clinical)

2. Feature Normalization

TempleCBE includes three standard feature scaling transformations:

  • min_max_norm(): Scales values to the range [0,1][0, 1].
  • z_norm(): Standardizes features to mean 00 and standard deviation 11.
  • range_norm(): Scales relative to combined distribution bounds across columns.
x <- c(10, 20, 30, 40, 50)

# Min-Max Normalization
min_max_norm(x)
#> [1] 0.00 0.25 0.50 0.75 1.00

# Z-Score Normalization
z_norm(x)
#> [1] -1.2649111 -0.6324555  0.0000000  0.6324555  1.2649111

3. Outlier Detection

detect_outliers() evaluates numeric vectors or data frame columns using Interquartile Range (IQR) thresholding, distinguishing between MILD (1.5 × IQR) and EXTREME (3.0 × IQR) outliers.

data_vals <- c(12, 14, 15, 14, 16, 15, 14, 45, 120)

# Detect mild and extreme outliers
detect_outliers(data_vals)
#> # A tibble: 2 × 4
#>   column value .outlier .outlier_type
#>   <chr>  <dbl> <fct>    <fct>        
#> 1 value     45 TRUE     EXTREME      
#> 2 value    120 TRUE     EXTREME

Summary

Combining SumNa(), features_percent_miss(), min_max_norm(), and detect_outliers() provides a reproducible, auditable workflow for preparing clinical data for downstream statistical modeling.
